title: Not as those without hope (1 Thessalonians 4:13)

cards: Two words in the King James Bible: "Jesus wept." He has just asked where they laid his friend Lazarus, and they've answered, come and see. In John's telling he is about to call Lazarus out of the grave.
He weeps anyway. Today's line is from Paul, writing to a young church in Thessalonica that had buried some of its own. This block met his sentence once already, read for what it says about the end.
Today, read it for grief. It's easy to hear it as an order to stop crying. Read slowly, it says something else.

teach.b: Here's the sentence: "But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope." First, read it slowly. Paul doesn't say: don't sorrow.
He says: don't sorrow even as, the same way as, those with no hope. Grief is assumed. He never asks them to stop crying; he asks what their tears are leaning on.
His attention is on the church he's writing to, not on anyone else's grief.
Second, the word asleep. Paul calls the dead them which are asleep. It's gentle, and it carries a hope inside it, because sleep is something you wake from.

He goes on: "For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him." Third, back to Lazarus. In John's story, Jesus weeps knowing what he is about to do.
The hope doesn't cancel the tears. It stands next to them.
That's the shape Paul is asking for: tears, with something underneath. Fourth, grief kept company.
Paul tells the church in Rome, "Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep." Not explain to them. Not hurry them along.
Weep with them. Christian grief, in these letters, is not quieter or tidier than anyone's. It cries, and it doesn't cry alone.

how: 1 Thessalonians 4:13–18 is among the readings offered in some churches' funeral services, and some Christians speak of the dead as having fallen asleep in Christ.

games.q: what does “not as those without hope” mean?
o: Paul's order to stop crying over the dead
a phrase about people who have lost their faith
Paul's phrase: grieve, but leaning on hope

games.q: not as those without hope — tap the pairs.
p: on the way to Lazarus's grave

s: Paul tells the Thessalonians not to grieve
he says don't sorrow "even as others which have no hope." grief is assumed.
Jesus wept on his way to Lazarus's grave
"Jesus wept," though in the story he was about to raise his friend. he reaches the grave three verses later.
Paul tells the Romans to cheer up those who weep
"weep with them that weep." he asks for company in grief, not a quick fix.

games.q: you're Paul. a young church writes that some of their own have died, and they're grieving and afraid. what's the first thing you say about their dead?
o: stop crying; it shows weak faith.
grieve, but not like those with no hope.
don't think about it; focus on the living.
games.why: "that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope." he doesn't forbid grief. he tells them what it can lean on.

practice: Bring to mind a loss, a person or something else you've had to let go of, and let yourself feel its weight without hurrying past it.
If you pray, hold it alongside Paul's words, them which are asleep; if not, hold it alongside one good thing that loss left in you, a habit, a laugh, a way of seeing.

Let the grief and the hope sit side by side, neither one winning. If grief feels too heavy to carry alone, or you're thinking of harming yourself, please call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Not as those without hope. Paul's phrase in First Thessalonians four: Christians grieve, and their grief leans on the hope of the resurrection.

orig.note: Greek: those who are sleeping, Paul's word for the dead in 1 Thessalonians 4:13. from the same verb comes koimētērion, a sleeping place: cemetery.

carryVoice: Your line: grieve, with hope. Tears come first, and the hope stands beside them. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.
For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him.
Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.
